relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: A city trapped in famine hears an impossible promise of food by tomorrow.
A royal officer cannot imagine the opening and is told he will see without eating.
Four excluded men sit at the gate between two forms of death.
They choose movement because stillness offers no safety.
At twilight they enter an enemy camp that has already emptied.
Fear has multiplied sound into armies and driven the besiegers away.
The camp remains full while its owners flee for life.
The starving men eat first, then hide wealth in the old reflex of scarcity.
Conscience turns private survival into public responsibility.
The city's excluded ones become its first messengers of abundance.
The word passes from gate to palace.
The king interprets hope through the memory of military traps.
A servant proposes verification with the few horses left alive.
The reconnaissance leaves before the city rushes out.
The road to Jordan confirms a panicked retreat.
The city pours into the camp, and food prices collapse from famine to plenty.
At the gate, unmanaged desperation tramples the officer.
The promised prices are repeated as fulfilled.
The officer's earlier disbelief is recalled.
He sees abundance but dies beneath the crowd.

contemplative_note: The people who save Samaria are the people Samaria kept outside. They are not fearless saints; they are hungry, excluded, practical, briefly secretive, and finally truthful. Good news becomes holy when it moves from private survival toward shared life.
